It runs no garbage collect. Live evidence shows manifest deletes are enabled (registry-cleanup's DELETEs return 202), so RegistryDeploy needs no change. Step 1 was dry-run read-only against the live registry. Close-out A5 records that DockerImages main must carry P11 before the deletion.

The registry-deletion procedure is accurate against the registry as deployed and covers D3/V10, but step 2's rm -rf is scoped only by $REPO from step 1's shell. In a fresh shell, which this environment forces because kubectl lives only in the iac sidecar, it forms `rm -rf .../v2/repositories/` against the prd registry pod, and step 3's check passes vacuously.

history.summary: F1 witnessed: step 2 run in a fresh iac shell formed `rm -rf .../v2/repositories/` against the live registry pod, and step 3 passed silently on an empty REPO. DockerImages a963dfd makes both steps read `${REPO:?set REPO to the repository}`, so they abort before running when REPO is unset or empty (re-run: exit 1 with the message, rm never formed; interactive bash skips the command). Done-record updated (AnsibleSpecs 57661ec).
